title: Chip-collateralized SPV leaseback - moving AI compute (and its debt) off the balance sheet
source: Public record + reporting: Amazon's proposed ~$8B SPV to spin out NVIDIA Grace Blackwell chips and lease them back (FT, 2026 - described as under discussion, NOT signed; outside investors hold the debt + up to ~10% equity, Amazon retains no ownership); Apollo + Blackstone's ~$35B 'AI XPV' hardware-collateralized vehicle for Anthropic (closed 9 Jun 2026 - SPV buys Broadcom-codesigned Google TPUs, Anthropic leases them back off its balance sheet, funded largely by insurance/annuity capital, Broadcom backstops senior tranches); Apollo-led ~$3.5B capital solution into Valor Compute Infrastructure (VCI) for a ~$5.4B GB200 triple-net lease to an xAI subsidiary (Jan 2026); NVIDIA naming Apollo among six institutions to mobilize >$500B of third-party AI-infra capital (Aug 2026); BIS warning on 'shadow borrowing'. Amazon cut assumed server life 6->5 yrs (early-2025 filing) on faster AI obsolescence. Overlay on the AI-capital-loop + datacenter-debt-SPV threads; structural edges only (no financial-core edges; dollar/debt/lease/collateral wording lives in notes). HONESTY: the closed Apollo/Blackstone (Anthropic) + Apollo/Valor (xAI) deals = FACT; the Amazon chip-SPV = REPORTED/UNCONFIRMED; there is NO confirmed Amazon<->Apollo deal - Apollo is the archetypal operator of the SAME mechanism, not a named Amazon counterparty; 'hiding data-center losses' is the popular framing - more precisely it is off-balance-sheet asset-light optics + residual-value-risk transfer, graded contested/interpretation.

edges.notes: REPORTED/UNCONFIRMED (FT 2026): Amazon in talks to spin ~$8B of NVIDIA Grace Blackwell chips already in its US data centers into an SPV and LEASE THEM BACK; the SPV issues debt to outside investors (who also get up to ~10% equity) and Amazon retains no ownership. Effect: AI buildout looks less capital-intensive on paper (assets rise slower, return-on-asset ratios look better) and residual-value/financing risk shifts to investors. 'Under discussion', not signed (reported-unconfirmed).

The structure funds AI-compute/datacenter capacity OFF the operator's balance sheet: the SPV owns the chips, the operator leases them, outside debt funds the purchase. It is the compute-side cousin of the real-estate off-balance-sheet datacenter SPVs (fact of the mechanism).

Apollo Global Management (with Blackstone) anchored the ~$35B 'AI XPV' hardware-collateralized vehicle (closed 9 Jun 2026) - one of the largest private-credit transactions on record; capital raised largely from insurance + annuity funds (fact).
Blackstone co-anchored the ~$35B AI XPV vehicle alongside Apollo (fact).
The SPV buys Broadcom-codesigned Google TPUs and LEASES them to Anthropic; the lease payments repay the debt, and holding the hardware in the SPV keeps ~$35B off Anthropic's balance sheet (fact).

Broadcom co-designs the TPUs the vehicle buys AND backstops payments on the senior tranches - the chip vendor underwriting the financing of its own chips, the purest vendor-adjacent-financing loop (fact; circularity read = interpretation).
AI XPV is the flagship instance of the chip-collateralized-SPV structure (fact).

Apollo-managed funds led a ~$3.5B capital solution into Valor Compute Infrastructure (VCI, a Valor Equity Partners fund) supporting its ~$5.4B acquisition-and-lease of GB200 compute to an xAI subsidiary via a TRIPLE-NET LEASE (Jan 2026) - powering a large Grok training cluster (fact).
VCI owns the NVIDIA GB200 GPUs and leases them to xAI (triple-net) - chips held in a vehicle, leased to the operator, off the operator's balance sheet (fact).
The Valor/xAI deal is another instance of the same lease-back structure (fact).

Sibling playbook: Meta's Hyperion datacenter uses a Blue Owl / Beignet off-balance-sheet SPV on the REAL-ESTATE side; chip-collateral SPVs do the same on the COMPUTE side - the off-balance-sheet AI-buildout pattern now spans both land and silicon (fact of parallel; ties the datacenter-debt-SPV block).

These vehicles are funded largely by PRIVATE CREDIT + INSURANCE/ANNUITY capital - pushing fast-depreciating GPU residual-value risk onto insurers' balance sheets. The BIS has warned about 'shadow borrowing' in these structures; Amazon itself cut assumed server life 6->5 years (early 2025) on AI obsolescence, which is exactly the residual-value risk being transferred (fact of funding + warning; systemic-risk read = interpretation).

NVIDIA named Apollo among SIX institutions tapped to mobilize >$500B of third-party capital for AI-infra buildout (Aug 2026) - the chip vendor helping orchestrate the financing that buys its chips; the circular-financing concern the map's capital-core tracks, now extended to the SPV layer (fact of the partnership; circularity framing = interpretation).

Chip-collateral leases carry the same core fragility as the neocloud refinancing wall: if GPU residual values fall faster than the lease amortizes, the collateral under the debt erodes - concentrated, correlated, and maturity-clustered (interpretation, labeled; ties the refinancing-wall block).
